stem.en: The Humboldt (Peru) Current runs north along the west coast of South America, bringing water from colder regions. What does it do to the coast beside it?

text.en: It cools the coast, as its water is cold.

feedback.en: Yes. A current tends to carry the warmth or cold of the place it came from, and this one came from a colder region.

text.en: It warms the coast, as all currents bring warmth.

feedback.en: Not all currents bring warmth. This one carries cold water, so it cools the coast.

text.en: It has no effect, as currents stay far out at sea.

feedback.en: Currents run along coasts and change their temperature, as the Gulf Stream does for Norway.

text.en: It warms the coast only in the hot months of the year.

feedback.en: Its water comes from colder regions, so it does not warm the coast.

explanation.en: The Humboldt (Peru) Current is a cold current. It brings water from colder regions, so it cools the coast it runs past. A current tends to carry the warmth or cold of the place it came from.

hints.en: Ask where the water in this current was before it started running north.
